view: The line this print trades on is the FY2026 revenue guide and the H2 ramp, not EPS. The evidence says the ramp did not happen in Q3, and the sell-side numbers still assume it did. The CEO floated $14-28M of Q3 Drone Dominance revenue in August. On 2026-09-15 Teal Drones landed outside the Gauntlet II top-5 leaderboard and was listed among the non-ranked close-quarters participants, so that Phase II order flow went to others. No sizeable Army Black Widow order has been announced in 2026. The Army bought 2,500+ Skydio X10Ds in March to keep competition alive, and Red Cat says it builds ahead of demand (inventory $84.8M at June 30). Driscoll's resignation has put the Army's drone push in doubt. The Navy is reassessing its USV requirements and Blue Ops shows no named orders (Euronaval, 2026-11-05). Unusual Machines, a component supplier to the FPV makers, saw Q3 revenue fall 17% from Q2. So a Q3 revenue miss against about $39M is likely, and a cut to the $150-180M guide (or its withdrawal) is the most likely outcome. The price has already moved hard on this: down 66% since August, at the 52-week low, about 25% of shares short and climbing, upside skew paid. The buy side's real bar is clearly far below the stale sell-side $151M. The reaction will turn on whether the reset guide and Q4/2027 visibility (Drone Dominance follow-ons, SRR, Steyr pro-forma) come in better or worse than a bar I cannot measure. A large miss, a guide cut, inventory or margin trouble and the Steyr cash call point down. A 'less bad than feared' reset into a crowded short points up. On balance the open slightly favours down, and not by enough to act on.

recommendation.reason: The fundamental evidence points to a Q3 revenue miss and a guide cut. Sell-side FY consensus of about $151M is stale, Teal is absent from the Gauntlet II leaderboard, and no large Army order has been announced. But the price has fallen 66% since August with about 25% of shares short, so I cannot show that the buy side's bar sits above the likely reset. The mechanism for a further drop is real, but whether it is priced cannot be shown either way, so it does not clear 65%.
recommendation.what_would_flip_it: Q3 revenue near or above $35-40M with the FY guide only trimmed (e.g. to ~$130M+) or reaffirmed, or a named large Q4 order (Drone Dominance follow-on, SRR, or a USV contract). Into 25% short interest that would gap the stock up sharply.

self_critique: My downside lean rests on stale sell-side numbers, but the buy side clearly stopped believing the $150M+ guide weeks ago: the stock lost two-thirds of its value since August, sits at its 52-week low, and has 25% of its shares short. When a well-telegraphed guide cut lands into that setup, it often clears the overhang and squeezes the shorts, especially if management uses the release to frame 2027 with Steyr pro-forma revenue and new product orders. The Nov 2025 analogue (-12.8% gap) came off a much higher starting valuation, so it may not apply.
